accepted_optimizations.basis: Synthetic CPU byte equivalence plus paired CPU timings for texture transfer, UBO, dirty ranges and mip geometry.
Fidelity fix; restored exact FP32 shader source after a reproducible synthetic mismatch.
Paired host comparisons with sanitizers and independent references. Results and scripts for bounds, feedback and pipelines in docs/evidence/s2arm-0437-review.
Presentation output and queue ownership under simulated completion, partial failure and shutdown. See docs/evidence/s2arm-0437-review/present. Correctness fixes; physical FPS unknown.
Platform correctness. Use Metal budget on macOS, retain the existing 512 MiB policy on iOS. No performance claim.

Remove redundant row copies and transposes when the widescreen classifier is called. Equivalent outputs, 792 existing checks, 24 NativeAOT triplets each on Linux x86-64 and macOS arm64. See matrices/README.md. Game and iPhone frame times unknown.

rejected_optimizations: Draft address indexing changed alias eviction order and mesh slot ownership.
Draft argument reuse missed indirect UBO texture metadata changes.
Weaker atomics and growing dirty-range footprint.
Draft draw-state shortcut omitted projection reset.
FP16 motion matching changed the selected vector on synthetic blocks.
Two partial feedback shortcuts slowed changing substitutions.
Additional blend-state filtering slowed cold/warm pipeline table cases versus 0444.

Four WidenSession shader-slot mask variants made heavily bound synthetic scans cheaper but increased the median for one bound slot per stage. See drafts/widen-mask (13 randomized triplets in each of five cases per series).

Prioritizing unseen stage coverage among equally urgent recorded pipeline rows increased modeled cumulative draw stalls in 28/144 scenarios with unchanged startup caps. No live policy change. See pipeline/warm-order.md.
Four GPU texture GOBs per group: 36 triplets with same-width A/A, 64 dispatches per sample; all five paired intervals include zero vs both controls. Keep production width one.
Direct lane-wise comparison of effective UBO caps on stable cache hits: +13.53% and +10.82% CPU time across binary orders on Linux. Preserve all invalidation semantics.
remaining_bottlenecks: Presentation queue scheduling, native frame pacing and actual displayed content
First-use pipeline compilation and residency measured separately from CPU key construction
Shader compilation and translation with legal homebrew workloads
next_axis: Track 0448 opt-in SDK compilation and 0449 iOS engine and Mac edge/RSS verification. Characterize effective UBO caps and reject unsafe invalidation. Repeat the GPU dispatch and equal-budget stage-order analysis before accepting any scheduling policy; investigate safe layer rotation under in-flight rendering.
legacy_note: First 21 entries are original host summaries. Their draft patch numbers describe historical experiments; numbers may differ from integrated engine patches. Cachegrind counters are on x86. The uncalibrated projections were withdrawn. No legacy entry establishes fidelity, A18 Pro frametime, GPU time, energy, RAM or FPS.

review_rule.definition: One completed independent candidate with no measurable reproducible improvement after the most recently accepted change. Inconclusive repeats of the same candidate count once. Blend-state filtering was rejected after 0444.
review_rule.counter_note: A measurement-only patch does not reset the performance rejection count. The four slot masks and one scheduler model are independent candidates. Superseded incorrect matrix trial is tracked while its repaired candidate is under comparison.

excluded_experiments: Per-frame clearing of borrowed resource tables: the exploratory analysis consulted a personal archive in conflict with the autonomous input constraint. All candidate patches, timings and prioritization from that investigation are excluded.
layer_rotation_review: iOS front adapter creates one layer and reuses it even across a display switch. No evidence of layer-object rotation as a steady-state iPhone performance bottleneck. Mac replacement and device mutation differ; do not assume an old residencySet can be recovered from the layer after a device change.
